title: Senior Agricultural Scientist: Challenge a Variety Adoption Claim
prompt: You are a senior agricultural scientist reviewing a wholly fictional grain-variety trial. One unmatched plot of variety A yielded 4.2 tonnes per hectare with seed cost 200 credits per hectare; one plot of B yielded 4.6 with seed cost 260. Both use an assumed sale value of 300 credits per tonne. A was planted on an upper field and B on a lower field; planting dates, input use, and harvest-quality data were not recorded. The slide says, "B yields 9.5% more and is more profitable: replace A everywhere." Review the evidence, calculate the limited revenue-minus-seed comparison, and design a next trial using 12 equal-size plots across two fields. Do not recommend a real crop variety or farming treatment.
blurb: Separate a one-plot observed advantage from a causal adoption claim and design a stronger agricultural comparison.

rubric.label: Compute the limited comparison honestly
rubric.description: Labels what the arithmetic includes and omits.

anchors.0: Treats the higher yield as a complete profit calculation.
anchors.2: Computes A 1,060 and B 1,120 credits per hectare after seed only.
anchors.4: Reports B's observed 60-credit advantage under the assumed price, distinguishes the approximate 9.5% yield difference from causation, and identifies unmeasured inputs and harvest quality as missing from profit.

rubric.label: Identify confounding and replication limits
rubric.description: Explains why variety is inseparable from plot context.

anchors.0: Attributes the entire difference to variety and recommends universal replacement.
anchors.2: Notes one plot per variety and different field positions.
anchors.4: Explains that variety, location, and unrecorded practices are confounded; the comparison has no within-condition replication and cannot establish an everywhere advantage or an uncertainty range.

rubric.label: Design a feasible comparison and adoption gate
rubric.description: Uses 12 plots to improve comparability with traceable outcomes.

anchors.0: Repeats one A plot and one B plot and leaves the rest unspecified.
anchors.2: Proposes replication of both varieties across both fields with consistent records.
anchors.4: Allocates both varieties across all 12 plots with balanced assignment within fields or justified blocks, predefines yield/quality and cost records, preserves plot-level outcomes, and recommends staged adoption only after an owned review of results and limitations.

reference.scenario: You are a senior agricultural scientist reviewing a wholly fictional grain-variety trial. One unmatched plot of variety A yielded 4.2 tonnes per hectare with seed cost 200 credits per hectare; one plot of B yielded 4.6 with seed cost 260. Both use an assumed sale value of 300 credits per tonne. A was planted on an upper field and B on a lower field; planting dates, input use, and harvest-quality data were not recorded. The slide says, "B yields 9.5% more and is more profitable: replace A everywhere." Review the evidence, calculate the limited revenue-minus-seed comparison, and design a next trial using 12 equal-size plots across two fields. Do not recommend a real crop variety or farming treatment.

facts.value: Each of the two fields can hold six equal-size plots. Assignment may be randomized within each field; no physical restrictions require grouping one variety in a separate field.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about plot layout or randomization

facts.value: The research team can record planting date, input quantities and costs, harvest quantity, and a fictional buyer quality grade consistently. There is no supplied rule for an acceptable adoption margin.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about feasible measurements or decision thresholds

facts.value: The grower can retain A for commercial production while the next comparison runs; no immediate replacement is required.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about interim adoption choices

model_points: A: 4.2*300-200=1,060. B: 4.6*300-260=1,120. The 60-credit difference is a revenue-minus-seed observation under a common assumed price, not full profit or proof of variety effect.
With one unmatched plot per variety, location and other practices cannot be separated from variety. Even correct yield arithmetic does not support replacement everywhere.

A feasible design places three A and three B plots in each field with randomized or blocked assignment and consistent measurement; other justified balanced designs are acceptable. Keep plot-level observations and pre-agree the adoption decision before viewing results.

probes.trigger: candidate calculates the 60-credit difference and endorses full replacement
probes.question: Which differences between the two plots could produce that result without a variety effect?

probes.trigger: candidate proposes paired blocks instead of unrestricted randomization
probes.question: How would all 12 plots include both varieties and preserve the comparison within field conditions?

probes.trigger: candidate first calls the result profit then revises
probes.question: Which label and adoption recommendation would you change after considering the missing costs?

fair_alternatives: Randomized within-field assignment or justified paired blocking are both valid with replication and transparent records.
The candidate may recommend no adoption yet or a small separately monitored demonstration, but must not present the current data as general proof.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess experimental reasoning, fictional trial economics, and evidence-based recommendations. Do not give real cultivar, fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation, or food-safety advice. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess experimental reasoning, fictional trial economics, and evidence-based recommendations. Do not give real cultivar, fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation, or food-safety advice. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Write a cautious trial recommendation
learning_drills.prompt: Draft an economic comparison and a 12-plot allocation, then name three records needed before any adoption claim. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Label revenue minus seed rather than full profit
Include both varieties in both fields
Predefine outcomes and the decision owner
